title: Symmetry of Tor for modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M,N$ be $R$-modules, and let $i\ge0$. There is a natural $R$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(N,M)$, where both Tor modules are defined by the homology of a projective resolution tensored with the other module [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), lines 18534-18618, including the functoriality paragraph

proof.text: Setup. Choose projective resolutions $\cdots\to P_1\xrightarrow{d^P_1}P_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ of $M$ and $\cdots\to Q_1\xrightarrow{d^Q_1}Q_0\xrightarrow{\eta}N\to0$ of $N$; by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(M,N)\cong H_i(P_\bullet\otimes_RN)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(N,M)\cong H_i(Q_\bullet\otimes_RM)$ canonically ($\iota_{P,N}$, $\iota_{Q,M}$), independently of the choices. Form the double complex $A_{i,j}=P_i\otimes_RQ_j$ ($i,j\ge0$) [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with $d_{i,j}=d^P_i\otimes1_{Q_j}:A_{i,j}\to A_{i-1,j}$ and $\delta_{i,j}=1_{P_i}\otimes d^Q_j:A_{i,j}\to A_{i,j-1}$. Then $d\circ d=(d^Pd^P)\otimes1=0$, $\delta\circ\delta=1\otimes(d^Qd^Q)=0$, and $\delta_{i-1,j}d_{i,j}=d^P_i\otimes d^Q_j=d_{i,j-1}\delta_{i,j}$ by functoriality of $\otimes$ in each factor; all maps are $R$-linear.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof, first paragraph, lines 18542-18555 (there with free resolutions $F_\bullet$, $G_\bullet$; only the flatness of the terms (step 2) and the lifting of maps (step 7) are used, both of which hold for projective resolutions)

proof.text: Rows and columns are exact in positive degrees. Each $Q_j$ is projective, hence flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. For $i\ge1$ the sequence $P_{i+1}\to P_i\to P_{i-1}$ is exact (for $i=1$: $P_2\to P_1\to P_0$; exactness of the resolution [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]), so by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] applied with the flat module $Q_j$, $P_{i+1}\otimes Q_j\to P_i\otimes Q_j\to P_{i-1}\otimes Q_j$ is exact: row $j$ of $A$ is exact at $A_{i,j}$ for all $i\ge1$. Symmetrically, each $P_i$ is flat and $Q_{j+1}\to Q_j\to Q_{j-1}$ is exact for $j\ge1$, so column $i$ is exact at $A_{i,j}$ for all $j\ge1$. Hence $A$ satisfies hypotheses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-cokernel-homology-iso].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof, second paragraph, lines 18557-18563 ('Since each $G_j$ is free, and hence flat we see that each row of the double complex is exact except in homological degree 0 ...')

proof.text: The two cokernel complexes. Since $P_1\xrightarrow{d^P_1}P_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] (tensoring with $Q_j$) shows that $P_1\otimes Q_j\to P_0\otimes Q_j\xrightarrow{\varepsilon\otimes1}M\otimes Q_j\to0$ is exact, so $\varepsilon\otimes1_{Q_j}$ induces an isomorphism $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_j=\operatorname{Coker}(d_{1,j})\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_RQ_j$. Under these isomorphisms the differential induced by $\delta_{0,j}=1_{P_0}\otimes d^Q_j$ becomes $1_M\otimes d^Q_j$, because $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes d^Q_j)=\varepsilon\otimes d^Q_j=(1\otimes d^Q_j)\circ(\varepsilon\otimes1)$. So $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet\cong M\otimes_RQ_\bullet$ as chain complexes [def-weil-pbc-chain-complex-tensor-module] (the tensor complex with factors in the other order, which is defined in the same way). In exactly the same way, $Q_1\to Q_0\xrightarrow{\eta}N\to0$ exact and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] give $A^{\mathrm{up}}_i=\operatorname{Coker}(\delta_{i,1})\xrightarrow{\sim}P_i\otimes_RN$ via $1_{P_i}\otimes\eta$, compatible with the differentials $d^P_i\otimes1$: $A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet\cong P_\bullet\otimes_RN$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof, third paragraph, lines 18565-18576 (computation of $R(A)_\bullet=M\otimes_RG_\bullet$ and $U(A)_\bullet=F_\bullet\otimes_RN$)

proof.text: Comparison. By step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-cokernel-homology-iso] gives $R$-linear isomorphisms $\theta^A_i:H_i(A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_i(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$ for all $i\ge0$; with step 3 this is an $R$-linear isomorphism $H_i(P_\bullet\otimes_RN)\cong H_i(M\otimes_RQ_\bullet)$ (homology of isomorphic complexes being isomorphic [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof, display lines 18577-18589, third equality, 'Here the third equality is Lemma lemma-no-spectral-sequence'

proof.text: Swapping the factors. The isomorphisms $\tau_j=\tau_{M,Q_j}:M\otimes_RQ_j\to Q_j\otimes_RM$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm] satisfy $\tau_{j-1}\circ(1_M\otimes d^Q_j)=(d^Q_j\otimes1_M)\circ\tau_j$ by its naturality clause (with $f=1_M$, $g=d^Q_j$), so they form an isomorphism of chain complexes $M\otimes_RQ_\bullet\cong Q_\bullet\otimes_RM$ and induce $R$-linear isomorphisms $H_i(M\otimes_RQ_\bullet)\cong H_i(Q_\bullet\otimes_RM)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof, display lines 18577-18589, fifth equality, 'the fifth equality uses the isomorphism $V\otimes W=W\otimes V$ of the tensor product'

proof.text: The isomorphism. Define $\sigma_i(M,N):\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(M,N)\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(N,M)$ as the composite $\iota_{Q,M}^{-1}\circ H_i(\tau_\bullet)\circ\theta^A_i\circ\iota_{P,N}$, reading $\theta^A_i$ through the identifications of step 3, of the $R$-linear isomorphisms of steps 1, 4 and 5 and [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. It is an $R$-linear isomorphism.

Seven steps follow the proof of 00M3: the double complex P⊗Q, exactness of rows/columns by flatness of projectives, identification of the two cokernel complexes by right exactness of ⊗, the 00M1 comparison, the swap V⊗W≅W⊗V, the composite, and the functoriality paragraph (lifts of φ, ψ, the morphism α⊗β of double complexes, the 00M1 functoriality and Tor maps via lifts). Remark 00M2 (signs) is not needed: any isomorphism is natural as constructed. Statement kept. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-cokernel-homology-iso (00M1, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm (Mathlib leaf), lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-lift (Mathlib leaf).
